domain: Whether literary critics who champion 'plain style' as democratic and anti-elitist can defend that judgment without themselves performing the very interpretive connoisseurship they claim plain style dispenses with
topic: Whether literary critics who champion 'plain style' as democratic and anti-elitist can defend that judgment without themselves performing the very interpretive connoisseurship they claim plain style dispenses with

movement.gist: State the standard case for plain style: critics from Orwell onward have praised unadorned prose as the vehicle of democratic self-government, arguing it needs no specialist to unlock it.

Turn the theory on the critic making the argument: the very act of identifying 'plainness' as a virtue, distinguishing it from mere flatness or naivety, is a discriminating judgment that requires trained taste — the critic who praises plainness is exercising the expertise plainness is supposed to make unnecessary.

Manage the recursion openly: examine whether this self-implication sinks the argument or merely relocates it — perhaps the critic's expertise is compatible with democratic prose if it's expertise in service of others' judgment rather than substitute for it; but every attempt to specify what that service looks like (which examples count as 'plain,' which readers count as competent judges) turns out to require the same discriminating authority under a different name. This is where the real subject of the essay comes into view: not which prose style serves democracy, but whether any critical vocabulary can describe that service without smuggling expertise back in through the selection of examples and terms.

Inhabit the loop: the critic writing this very essay is doing exactly what's under examination — selecting terms, ranking styles, adjudicating what counts as democratic prose — and must continue anyway, since refusing to judge is itself a judgment, and the refusal doesn't exit the loop, it just relocates the critic inside it once more.

primary.axis: plain style as democratic transparency vs. plain style as itself a cultivated, expert taste
poles: plain prose lets ordinary readers judge for themselves, unmediated by expertise
recognizing and praising 'plainness' is a trained aesthetic judgment no less expert than any other

secondary.axis: the critic's vocabulary vs. the critic's position
poles: the critic can rename or renounce expertise
renaming expertise does not remove the critic's function

tension_system.interaction: the secondary tension shows why the primary one cannot be settled by better word choice — the critic's authority survives any vocabulary chosen to disclaim it

family_realization.note: Passage executes 'Self-Application' perfectly. Expert (author) voices skepticism of expertise itself while demonstrating it. Recursion managed in open: 'I have ranked Orwell...the discriminating work, done in plain view, in the act of warning against it.' Ends inside loop with both debts unpaid.

ending_behavior.note: 'Open Ledger' precisely realized. Final paragraph enumerates what each side owes: democrat owes account of taste needing no taster; skeptic owes reason his exposure isn't connoisseur's verdict. Aperture widens—neither debt paid, refusal suspended explicitly.

voice_consistency.note: Comparative Synthesist throughout: triangulates Orwell's position, the classical rhetorician's, the modern critic's, the translator defense, the author's own implication. Concrete particular: tea-stained memo. Uneven polish: rhetorical questions, nested syntax, earned formality. No generic AI register.

distractor_efficiency.note: Q1(D): stance_misread trap—author implicates expertise as real, not fraudulent. Q3(B): framework_import trap—readers must recognize the democrat's claim author then undercuts. Q7(C): adjacent_answer trap—addresses clarity, not who certifies it. Q8(B): example_promotion trap—biographical detail ≠ thesis refutation. Strong.

explanation_quality.note: Every wrong option tied to passage mechanisms with precision. Q2(B) notes the border metaphor 'denies exactly this neutral outside position.' Q5(A) identifies straw_version: 'passage never claims plain prose hides ornament.' Q6(D) cites 'stance' failure. Specific, locatable, never generic.

answers.reasoning: Passage's core thesis: no critical vocabulary can name that service without performing authority it disowns.
Border metaphor shows any neutral description already presupposes evaluative position inside judgment.
Author undermines this claim, showing specialist judgment always intervenes despite appearing unnecessary.
Analogy raised as graceful defense, then shown to collapse when demanded to be specific.
Text explicitly states the eye that certifies plainness has been trained to certify.
Never claimed critic secretly prefers ornate prose; irrelevant to stated failure reasons.
If untrained readers judge identically to critics, connoisseurship claim weakens; B highlights disagreement among experts instead.
A descriptive vocabulary avoiding evaluative authority would refute the thesis that naming always performs authority.
